story.head: One power play bites, one doesn’t
paras: The Blues won the teams’ first meeting this season, 4-0 in Dallas on Oct 2. The Stars (15-7-2) lost 3-1 to Nashville on Wednesday, and the Blues (13-9-3) lost 3-2 in a shootout to the Islanders the same night. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Stars second (tied for seventh in the NHL) and the Blues sixth (tied for 15th). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.
The Stars’ record (.667) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.593), largely because they’re 9-4 in one-goal games. The Blues’ record (.580) is about what their chances are worth.

The Stars play slow, tight games (lowest) and take more penalties than they draw (32nd). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), so the Stars are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Blues’ shots. Dallas has allowed 2.38 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Blues, they get the league’s best looks (1st), keep things calm after the whistle (lowest) and rarely ice the puck (2nd). The Stars’ power play bites, but the Blues’ doesn’t.

Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 18 A / 28 P in 24 GP) leads the Stars in scoring, with six goals in nine games against St. Louis since 2023-24. Jason Robertson (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 24 GP) isn’t far behind. For the Blues, Robert Thomas (5 G / 20 A / 25 P in 25 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eleven points in his last five games. Mason McTavish (9 G / 6 A / 15 P in 25 GP) has a team-high nine goals.

Jake Oettinger (13-5-1 / .912 SV% in 19 GS) has been a rock in net for Dallas and is expected to start. Joel Hofer (10-6-2 / .920 SV% in 18 GS) has been a rock in net for St. Louis and is expected to start.
At home, Jim Montgomery likes to send Toropchenko, Walker and Johnston out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Kiviranta, Faksa and Perron.
